title: 2005 HMMT February General Round 2 Problem 2
statement:
Find three real numbers \(a<b<c\) satisfying:

\[\begin{aligned}
a+b+c & =21 / 4 \\
1 / a+1 / b+1 / c & =21 / 4 \\
a b c & =1
\end{aligned}\]

solutions.text:
\(1 / 4,1,4\)
By inspection, one notices that if \(b\) is a number such that \(b+1 / b=17 / 4\), then \(a=1, c=\) \(1 / b\) will work. Again by inspection (or by solving the quadratic \(b^{2}-17 b / 4+1=0\) ), one finds \(b=1 / 4\) or 4 , so the numbers are \(1 / 4,1\), and 4 .
Alternative Solution: Note that \(a b+b c+c a=a b c(1 / a+1 / b+1 / c)=21 / 4\), so \(a, b\), and \(c\) are the roots of the polynomial \(x^{3}-21 x^{2} / 4+21 x / 4-1\), which factors as \(\frac{1}{4}(x-1)(x-4)(4 x-1)\), giving the same answer.
